_comment: What each operation costs, in credits. One credit is one penny.
An operation is charged when it costs this instance something to run: a
model call, or a third party we are billed for per request. Anything that
only touches this instance's own storage is 0, because it has no marginal
cost and charging for it taxed exactly the behaviour the product wants
more of. Abuse control for those is auth.CheckPostRate, not the price.
This is an operator's file. Edit it, or drop a pricing.json in the data
directory to override without rebuilding, or set the env var named on any
line to override that one. Env wins, then the data directory, then this.
label is what the cost table on /pricing and /wallet says. An operation
with no entry here is not published and charges 1 credit, which a test

operations.label: Travel time between two places
operations.note: routes_eta. Google Routes, 0.38p at Essentials (£3.76/1k after 10k free), 0.75p at Pro. We ask for traffic, which may bill at Pro — priced to cover it. The op id keeps the old name so an operator's existing override and usage history survive the rename

operations.label: Turn-by-turn directions
operations.note: Google Routes asking for steps and the road's shape, which is more than an ETA and bills higher — 1.14p at Enterprise

operations.label: Agent (standard)
operations.note: An agent run may fan out across tools, so it costs more than a chat turn

operations.label: Agent (premium)
operations.note: Routes to Anthropic where the rest use the default provider, an order of magnitude more per token. At 9 it was priced 29% above standard for 10-20x the cost

operations.label: App build (AI)
operations.note: Was 100 — a pound, six times the next most expensive thing on the menu, for less model than an agent run

operations.label: App edit (AI)
operations.note: The model call only. Manual editing at /apps/<slug>/edit is free

operations.label: WhatsApp conversation
operations.note: Twilio bills WhatsApp by the 24-hour conversation rather than the message, so this is charged once per window and the rest of the thread is free. Cheaper than a text because it costs us less and cannot be sent cold — the other person has to write first

operations.label: Text message (per segment)
operations.note: Twilio: under a penny to a US mobile, ~4p to a UK one, and charged per 160-character segment. A markup that would be silly on a search is the point here — a text cannot be unsent, and the number's reputation is shared by everybody on the instance. Ten pence makes a spam run cost real money before any of the other limits are reached

operations.label: Send message
operations.note: Local user to local user. "Message" not "mail": sending a real email is charged as external_email
